# Results -- Study 518 (Time-Series-Momentum) on real yfinance cross-asset panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen
(2012) time-series momentum -- trade each asset long if its OWN trailing 12-month return is
positive else short, inverse-vol-scale each position to a common risk target (capped leverage),
and average across a diversified cross-asset ETF basket. One execution lag (form on the
month-end close, hold the next month). As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 4740 days x 12 tickers | `9c13724a40d6` |
| Period covered | 2007-03-01 -- 2025-12-30 | -- |
| Monthly bars | 226 | -- |
| TSMOM holding months | 213 (2008-03 -- 2025-11) | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close (auto_adjust=True). Basket: 12 cross-asset ETFs
spanning five asset classes -- equity (SPY, EFA, EEM, IWM), bonds (TLT, IEF, LQD), commodities
(DBC, USO), gold (GLD), FX (UUP, FXE). The common window starts March 2007 because DBC / UUP /
FXE list in 2006-2007. One-way cost 10bps x turnover per rebalance + 50bps/yr borrow on the net
short notional.

**Survivorship bias -- named on the SIGNAL axis (not hidden in tradability):** the basket is
broad ETFs *still trading in 2026*, chosen ex post. Time-series momentum's *own-sign*
construction makes survivorship far MILDER than a cross-sectional equity sort -- a falling ETF
is *shorted*, never deleted, so there is no missing-loser-leg channel. But the vehicle list
itself excludes any ETF that closed, and no surviving fund had a terminal blow-up, so any TSMOM
premium reported here is a mild upper bound.

## Synthetic positive control (engine faithfulness -- NOT a real-tape claim)

A deterministic synthetic panel with a planted persistent own-asset trend. The engine must
score ~0 at the null and rise monotonically as the planted trend grows.

| Planted own-trend | Portfolio mean (ann) | HAC *t* |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.00 (null) | -0.2% | -0.13 |
| 0.15 | +7.4% | +3.66 |
| 0.30 | +15.4% | +6.31 |
| 0.50 | +23.6% | +8.80 |

Monotone in the planted trend; across 20 random seeds the null mean *t* is **-0.31** (not the
single-seed -0.13 above) and **0%** of seeds exceed |t|>2 -- a faithful, well-sized detector.
**This is a power check only; it is never cited to support the real-tape stamp.**

## The honest test -- real TSMOM on the cross-asset basket

### Vol-scaled book (inverse-vol to a common target, capped leverage) -- the canonical MOP recipe

| Statistic | Gross | Net (costs + borrow) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean return (ann) | **+3.09%/yr** | +2.68%/yr |
| Vol (ann) | 7.9% | 7.9% |
| Sharpe (ann) | +0.392 | +0.340 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+1.611** | +1.396 |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 53.5% | -- |
| Max drawdown | -19.0% | -19.5% |
| Worst month | -7.9% | -- |
| Avg turnover | 13.5%/mo | -- |
| Avg short notional | 49.8% | -- |
| **Placebo p-value** | **0.005** | -- |

### Equal-notional book (sign only, no vol-scaling)

| Statistic | Gross | Net (costs + borrow) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean return (ann) | **+1.54%/yr** | +1.20%/yr |
| Sharpe (ann) | +0.198 | +0.154 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+0.788** | +0.613 |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 55.4% | -- |
| Max drawdown | -25.1% | -26.0% |
| Worst month | -7.7% | -- |
| Avg turnover | 12.1%/mo | -- |

- The vol-scaled TSMOM book earns **+3.09%/yr** gross at HAC *t* = **+1.611** -- a positive,
  economically sensible trend premium, but the one-sample *t* **does not clear the desk's bar of
  2**. The sign-shuffle placebo *p* = **0.005** (robust to ~0.005 across 10 RNG seeds) says the
  own-trend link is *real structure* -- the portfolio is far better than randomly flipping each
  position's sign -- yet the noisy 18-year tape leaves the one-sample *t* short of significance.
- **Robustness is fragile.** Sweeping the lookback the gross *t* is 9m: **+2.02**, 12m:
  **+1.61**, 15m: **+0.45** -- it straddles the bar and the canonical 12-month spec sits below
  it. Neither half of the sample clears 2 alone (first half *t* = 0.78, second half *t* = 1.47).
  Vol-target choice barely moves the *t* (0.10/0.15/0.20 -> 1.59/1.61/1.62).
- **Vol-scaling earns its keep.** Inverse-vol sizing roughly doubles the Sharpe (0.39 vs 0.20)
  and the *t* (1.61 vs 0.79) versus an equal-notional sign book, and halves the drawdown
  (-19% vs -25%) -- exactly the Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen claim that risk-balancing across asset
  classes is what makes trend a diversified premium rather than an equity-beta proxy.

## Year-by-year vol-scaled TSMOM (gross)

| Year | TSMOM | Year | TSMOM |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| 2008 | +4.8% | 2017 | +17.4% |
| 2009 | -8.7% | 2018 | -18.2% |
| 2010 | +0.5% | 2019 | +12.4% |
| 2011 | -0.7% | 2020 | -1.1% |
| 2012 | +2.5% | 2021 | +4.4% |
| 2013 | +7.9% | 2022 | +10.3% |
| 2014 | +16.1% | 2023 | -3.0% |
| 2015 | +3.6% | 2024 | +9.1% |
| 2016 | -8.7% | 2025 | +8.6% |

TSMOM shone in the 2008 crisis (+4.8% while equities collapsed -- the "crisis alpha" trend funds
sell) and again in the 2022 rates/commodity trend (+10.3%), but bled in the choppy reversals of
2009, 2016 and 2018 (-18.2%). The premium is real-looking but thin and regime-dependent.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** Vol-scaled TSMOM earns +3.09%/yr gross at HAC *t* = **+1.611** with a
  sign-shuffle placebo *p* = **0.005**. The placebo says the own-trend link is genuine structure
  (not data-mining), and the synthetic control proves the engine *would* score a clean *t* if the
  trend were strong -- but the canonical 12-month one-sample *t* does **not** clear the desk's bar
  of 2, and it is fragile to the lookback (2.02 / 1.61 / 0.45 at 9 / 12 / 15 months). Per house
  rules, strong literature (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012) plus a sub-2 *t* is **WEAK**, never REAL.
- **Tradability -- FRAGILE.** Net of 10bps x turnover + 50bps/yr borrow the book still earns
  **+2.68%/yr** at a **0.34 net Sharpe** with a contained **-19.5%** drawdown and modest
  ~14%/mo turnover -- genuinely positive net, unlike most factors on the desk. But the edge
  rests on persistent shorting (~50% short notional, borrow + recall risk), leveraged inverse-vol
  sizing, and a 12-asset diversification that a retail book cannot cheaply replicate; with a
  signal *t* below 2 it is a thin, fragile carry, not a robustly investable one.
- **Vol-scaling vs equal-notional (3rd axis) -- CONFIRMED.** Inverse-vol risk-balancing roughly
  doubles the Sharpe (0.39 vs 0.20) and the *t* (1.61 vs 0.79) and halves the drawdown
  (-19% vs -25%) versus a naive sign-only book. The Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen insight -- that
  risk-balancing across asset classes is what turns own-asset trend into a diversified premium --
  holds on this tape.
